description: Bristol-Myers Co. and Squibb Corp. merged in 1989 to form what’s now one of the world’s largest pharmaceutical companies. Bristol-Myers Squibb develops, licenses, manufactures, and delivers biopharmaceutical products for the treatment and management of diseases including HIV/AIDS, cancer, blood disorders, and cardiovascular and fibrotic conditions.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies To Work For – Europe
rankings.itemDescription: U.S. business Bristol Myers Squibb was founded in the early 1800s and aims to combine the reach and resources of a global pharma company with the entrepreneurial spirit and agility of a biotech firm. European sites in Germany, Ireland, Switzerland, Belgium, France and the U.K. host employees. Global flexibility guidelines aim to optimize working patterns for each individual around their role, family responsibilities, health needs and personal preferences. A sense of purpose runs through the company, from influencing EU policies to philanthropy; an employee giving program, administered by the BMS Foundation, doubles staff's financial contributions to eligible charitable organizations. In 2022 the organization donated £2 million to NHS cancer services, charities and patient groups.

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription: Last year, the New York–based Bristol-Myers Squibb tied ESG initiatives to executive compensation in a first for the pharmaceutical company. That effort came after a 2022 initiative to have 25% of clinical trials in diverse communities. CEO Giovanni Caforio chairs the 11-member board, of whom 10 are independent directors. Other directors include Peter Arduini, president and CEO of GE Healthcare, and Paula Price, who most recently served as Macy’s chief financial officer. Deepak Bhatt, director of Mount Sinai Heart, is the latest board appointment, tapped for his extensive cardiovascular research and clinical trial expertise. In June, the board approved the acquisition of cancer drug company Turning Point Therapeutics for $76 a share in a deal totaling $4.1 billion. The firm is still scouting for new M&A deals, Caforio said in its latest earnings call, as the pharma giant tries to offset a sales loss from two drugs that lost patent exclusivity last year. Also in 2022, the company laid off roughly 170 employees due to redundancies from its 2019 acquisition of Celgene. Women and minorities separately make up 36% of the board. Current chief operating officer Christopher Boerner will succeed Caforio when he steps down in November.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The New York City–based pharmaceutical giant had a lackluster 2022, dropping 13 spots on the Fortune 500 as its revenue decreased by 0.5% and profits dropped 9.5% from the prior year.

  • In 2022, Revlimid, a cancer drug, lost exclusivity in the U.S., which allowed generics to eat into its market share. Once a company blockbuster, the drug saw a 22% decrease in revenue from $12.8 billion in 2021 to approximately $10 billion in 2022.

  • Bristol-Myers Squibb’s other top drugs, Eliquis, an anticoagulant, and Opdivo, used for chemotherapy, brought in 21% and 15% more revenue, respectively, for 2022.

  • The company faces a steep patent cliff ahead as exclusivity for Eliquis and Opdivo is set to expire in 2028, and BMS is actively investing to find another drug to add to its portfolio, spending $9.5 billion in 2022 on research and development.

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription:
The board at pharmaceutical company Bristol-Myers Squibb scored high on age dispersion, and for having a high number of senior independent nonexecutive directors. Bristol-Myers Squibb’s board has three current CEOs, including its own, Giovanni Caforio, and Peter Arduini, CEO of GE Healthcare. Also on the board is Derica Rice, former CVS Health EVP and president of CVS Caremark, the pharmacy benefits management (PBM) business.

Though the company is facing a patent cliff, analysts are optimistic that BMS’s strong pipeline and cash flow will help carry the company in the long run. In 2021 BMS brought in $46.4 billion in revenue, exceeding its annual target and registering 9% year-on-year growth. The company also reported strong performance on supply-chain reliability and COVID-19 response, with a 99% vaccination rate among its employees in the U.S. and Puerto Rico. BMS published its first global diversity and inclusion report in 2021, setting goals to achieve gender parity at the executive level globally and to double the number of Black and Latinx/Hispanic executives in the U.S. by the end of 2022.

BMS plans to leverage up to $45 billion in free cash flow in the next two years to execute a capital allocation strategy prioritizing business development and returns to shareholders. The company recently executed a $5 billion accelerated share repurchase agreement during the first quarter, part of a multiyear $15 billion buyback program.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The New York City–based pharmaceutical company delivered strong financial results in 2021, with total revenue growing 9% year over year to $46.4 billion. Bristol-Myers Squibb enjoyed strong sales for drugs like Revlimid and Opdivo, used in the treatment of certain cancers; and Eliquis, an anticoagulant. Its product-development pipeline also looks healthy: In 2021, the company obtained more than 20 regulatory approvals for new medicines.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: The New Jersey–based drugmaker jumped up 209 places on this year’s Global 500 list—with 62.6% revenue growth—because of the additional sales that came with its $74 billion acquisition of Celgene in 2019. Sales of BMS’s anticoagulant Eliquis and its immuno-oncology drug Yervoy also showed strong growth in 2020. The company won 13 additional drug or formulation approvals in the U.S., European Union, and Japan last year; it also acquired MyoKardia, a biotech focused on cardiovascular diseases, for $13.1 billion in November 2020.
